facts.text: Founded May 3 1828 by Colonel Rezin Davis and Samuel Morrison, Morristown was named by Mary Davis in honor of minister Morrison.
After the Knightstown Railroad arrived in 1848 and the Cincinnati, Hamilton & Dayton Railroad in 1866, Morristown blossomed into a hub for pottery, barrels, bricks and canned goods.
Morristown’s streets were laid out in a classic grid, with Main, North, South, Poplar and Jackson forming the town’s core.
The 1853 Morristown Academy building stands today as a testament to the town’s early commitment to education and historic preservation.
Nestled in a scenic valley along Brookville State Road, Morristown lies about 30 miles southeast of Indianapolis.
